Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system

Class ProcessRunner

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.ProcessRunner
public final class ProcessRunner extends Object
A minimal ProcessBuilder helper for running external commands and capturing their output.

The Linux system backends in this package (DisplayService, Opener, PrivilegedRunner, ThermalService, ...) shell out to standard desktop tools (xrandr, xdg-open, gio, pkexec, sensors, getconf). This class centralises that plumbing so callers never touch raw streams.

Everything is best-effort: a missing executable, a non-zero exit or a timeout is reported through the returned ProcessRunner.Result instead of being thrown, so the desktop degrades gracefully when a tool is not installed (for example, xrandr is useless under a Wayland compositor).

No JNI/JNA and no external libraries are used; this is pure JDK.

      public static ProcessRunner.Result run(List<String> command, long timeout, TimeUnit unit, File workingDir)
      Runs a command, capturing stdout and stderr on separate gobbler threads (so a full pipe can never deadlock the child) and enforcing a timeout.

    • run

      public static ProcessRunner.Result run(List<String> command, String stdin, long timeout, TimeUnit unit, File workingDir)
      Runs a command, optionally writing stdin to the child's standard input, capturing stdout and stderr and enforcing a timeout. Used by UserService to feed chpasswd.
      Parameters:
      command - the command and arguments
      stdin - text to write to the child's stdin, or null for none
      timeout - how long to wait for the process to exit
      unit - the timeout unit
      workingDir - optional working directory (null = inherit)
      Returns:
      the captured ProcessRunner.Result; never null

    • run

      public static ProcessRunner.Result run(List<String> command, String stdin, long timeout, TimeUnit unit, File workingDir, Consumer<String> lineSink)
      Runs a command, optionally writing stdin to the child's standard input, capturing stdout and stderr and enforcing a timeout. While the child runs, every stdout line is also handed to lineSink as soon as it arrives (on the gobbler thread), so callers can render live progress instead of waiting for the buffered result.
      Parameters:
      command - the command and arguments
      stdin - text to write to the child's stdin, or null for none
      timeout - how long to wait for the process to exit
      unit - the timeout unit
      workingDir - optional working directory (null = inherit)
      lineSink - optional per-stdout-line callback (null = buffer only)
      Returns:
      the captured ProcessRunner.Result; never null
